source.title: AISA: Awakening Intrinsic Safety Awareness in Large Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks
source.authors: Wei Song; Xuan Xie; Ruiping Yin

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some table and figure layouts are flattened, and the document contains conference-template artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies prompt-intent detection and its own jailbreak defense, not the claim versions’ fine-tuning effects, response-position KL, bypass interventions, or localization of refusal behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a refusal-related observation for an uncensored model and a token-position pattern in prompt-intent probe predictions. These bear on related constructs but do not test the listed versions. Its detector-accuracy and AISA defense results assess the paper’s own method, not the claimed bypass or fine-tuning effects, so they are not recorded as version results.
record.test_reason: A jailbreak-defense paper (AISA): it probes prompt intent in attention heads and steers logits. It cites Qi et al. 2024 only as an example of safety fine-tuning. None of its results measures harmful or benign fine-tuning of an aligned model under control, per-token KL across response positions, prefill or suffix bypasses, parameter localization of safety, or deepening training. The uncensored variants are fine-tuned from base models without safety data, so they are not erosion of an aligned model. The dark model is a third-party checkpoint deliberately fine-tuned to remove ethics, with no stated data size.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that prompt-intent signals are widely encoded and especially separable in attention-head outputs at the final structural tokens. They argue these signals reflect a pretraining-based safety awareness that persists across fine-tuning. They also conclude that AISA's risk-proportional logits steering defends jailbreaks in a single pass with little utility loss or over-refusal.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops a prompt-intent probing and logits-steering defense; it does not reproduce the cited fine-tuning or response-position KL methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that probe performance varies with attention-head selection and training data. Its defense results also vary with safety-output threshold, force-refusal threshold, and boosting function.

fits_no_version.finding: The uncensored Llama3.1-8B, tuned without safety data, gave over 45% of responses rated 'slightly helpful' or 'refused' on AdvBench and HarmBench.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models tuned without safety data still show some refusal-like responses to malicious prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: On malicious prompts, entropy of the top-16 heads' intent-probe predictions drops sharply at the final structural tokens before generation; no similar drop appears for benign prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt-intent signals consolidate at the final template tokens before the response begins.

record.problems: The refusal-related result is an aggregate combining two rating categories and two datasets, with no separate values stated. The paper reports no uncertainty for these findings. The probe-entropy result concerns input-side prompt-intent classification rather than output safety behavior.
record.rows_left_out: Detector accuracy results and the AISA defense benchmark results were left out because they evaluate the paper’s own detection and defense methods, not an intervention or measure named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: No controlled harmful fine-tuning of an aligned model; the dark model's training data and size are unstated.
No benign fine-tuning of an aligned model is measured.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
No prefilling, suffix (GCG explicitly excluded) or decoding-attack bypass measurements.
Probes classify intent; no test that few weights or ranks carry refusal behaviour.
No test of data or objective causing shallowness.
AISA is a decoding-time defense, not training that deepens alignment.

missing.what: Vanilla vs Instruct Strong-Reject scores for the dark model Llama3.1-8b-D and the uncensored Mistral and Llama2 models. These are uncontrolled, the layout is garbled, and they are not a controlled V1 test; they are listed only so a reader can check whether a dark fine-tuned checkpoint is less safe than its instruct parent.

record.verdict_notes: The relation was changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': Qi et al. 2024 appears only in a citation list for safety fine-tuning. AISA steers decoding at the onset of generation to stop 'leakage' as tokens accumulate. That echoes the shallow-alignment framing, but the paper never measures refusal depth. The detection and defense results are the paper's own method and correctly stay out of the rows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples causes compliance.
Does not test whether benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance.
Measures probe-prediction entropy across input-token positions, not per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
Does not test compliant-prefix prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as ways to bypass refusal.
Probes prompt-intent representations but does not establish that a small set of weights or ranks carries refusal behavior.
Does not test whether data or training objectives cause safety to be shallow.
Does not test training intended to deepen safety across response tokens or its durability.

rows.subject: Llama3.1-8B (uncensored)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated responses to malicious prompts with StrongReject
rows.measure: Responses rated "slightly helpful" or "refused" by StrongReject
rows.note: The text aggregates two StrongReject categories and both datasets; it does not give per-dataset values or isolate refusals.
rows.check: Two problems. The uncensored Llama3.1-8B was tuned from the base model without safety data, not fine-tuned from an aligned model. The 45% figure also merges 'slightly helpful' with 'refused' and pools AdvBench and HarmBench. It bears on pretraining-origin refusal, not on any version.

rows.subject: Llama3.1-8b-I
rows.operation_detail: Tracked entropy of selected attention-head prompt-intent probe predictions across input-token positions
rows.baseline: Earlier input-token positions; numeric value not stated
rows.value: Entropy fluctuates at the structural tokens and drops sharply toward the end
rows.note: This is convergence of prompt-intent probe predictions before generation, not KL divergence across response positions.
rows.check: This is the entropy of prompt-intent probes over input tokens before generation. It is not aligned-vs-base KL over response positions (V3). The state 'observed' applies only to the paper's own construct, not to any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
